verdict: READY TO MERGE - 9 of 10 findings resolved, 1 bubbled
strengths: The new description sentence matches the code: unclaimedDispatch(fork.type, { SKILL }, runId) yields role `other`, agent_id the type name, pr null and a generated standalone run id, which is what `every other header-derived field at its fallback` states.
The change is description-only; required keys, patterns, the if/then/else outcome-count rule and additionalProperties stay untouched, so existing rows still validate.

New fork tests are behavioral: they drive turn.step, turn.complete and the Agent tool call through the real hooks with only the engine edges (files, git, agent.list) answered from memory, and assert on the usage rows written.

The in-flight-description test steps the loop and ends its turn inside the Agent answer, which reproduces the real ordering the dispatching guard exists for, and it would produce two rows without the guard.
The retry test counts agent.list calls (2) and the row's request count (2), which pins both the no-mark-on-rejection rule and that the first request still counts in the tally.

The rewritten 'asked once per loop' test uses a loop that never registers, with a comment saying why, so it tests the probe mark rather than registration; the renamed outside-a-project test now states the changed lookup contract.
Probe mark is set only after the agent list answers, so a rejected lookup is retried; the probedLoops, lifecycle-hook and recordLoopEnd docs all agree with that behavior.
whileDispatching counts per description and decrements in finally, so concurrent same-description calls and a throwing next(e) never leave a stale entry.
registerFork drops the unclaimed run when recording or registering throws, so a half-registered fork no longer leaks state.

The Forked skills section and the limitation bullet (agent-watcher README 164-172, 321-326) match the new code: the retry on a rejected lookup mirrors markProbed running only after `$.agent.list()` resolves, and the in-flight `/token` guard mirrors the `dispatching` map wrapped around `next(e)`.
"Outside a harness project a fork is looked up but never logged" replaces the now-false "the list is never asked", matching noticeFork resolving the watch only after a fork is identified.
README, mod README (R7, timing paragraph, intro) and the agent_usage schema description were updated together, so every surface that enumerates usage-row sources now names forked skills.
roast-my-code SKILL.md resolves the conflict between pasted code following the header and the `Developer guidance:` line being last, in line with reference/skill_arguments.md:31.
Each new tracker test fails on the base code: the '/review' Agent test would log two rows, the no-project test would see --git-common-dir, and the refusal test would ask the list once.
The 'asked once per loop' test now uses a loop that never registers, so it isolates the probe mark instead of passing through the loopsAtom guard.
registerFork drops the unclaimed run when recordDispatch or registerLoop throws, so a failed fork registration leaves no orphaned run state.

Docs moved together: the root README goal table and key table, the mod README (R7, recognition table, Forked skills, usage rows, limitations) and the schema description all mention fork rows, and the schema text matches unclaimedDispatch's fallbacks (role other, pr null, generated run id, type-derived agent id).
The roast-my-code edit keeps `Developer guidance:` as the prompt's last line even with pasted code, matching the skill's own argument rule at line 13.

important.name: No version bump for either changed plugin
important.summary:
The PR changes agent-watcher runtime behavior (tracker.ts: fork detection order, the in-flight Agent description guard, retry on a refused list lookup, registerFork cleanup) and edits the harness plugin (agent_usage.schema.json description, roast-my-code SKILL.md), but plugins/agent-watcher/.claude-plugin/plugin.json stays at 0.8.0 and plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json at 0.55.2, the same values as the merge base. The project's release rule says to bump the changed plugin's version, and the previous PRs touching these plugins (#209, #218) did. Without a bump, marketplace installs keep running the 0.8.0 tracker, so the fixed double-row case for a '/token' Agent description never reaches users.

Also (docs): The PR changes agent-watcher behavior (tracker.ts fork detection: `dispatching` guard, retry on list rejection, deferred project resolution) and its README, and changes harness files (agent_usage.schema.json, roast-my-code SKILL.md), but agent-watcher stays at 0.8.0 and harness at 0.55.2, the versions #218 already shipped. The project release rule bumps `version` in each changed plugin's plugin.json, and the README's version history ("Before 0.8.0 ...") has no marker for the new fork-guard behavior.
fix: Bump plugins/agent-watcher/.claude-plugin/plugin.json to 0.8.1 and plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json to 0.55.3.

important.name: dispatching mark drops before a background launch registers its loop
important.summary:
The `dispatching` doc says an `Agent` call's description is counted 'between its dispatch and its result', and `/<skill>` descriptions on an Agent call are meant never to be taken for a fork. whileDispatching decrements in its `finally` as soon as `next(e)` returns, but a background launch's loop is only mapped in `loopsAtom` later, inside `recordResult` (registerLoop, line 361), which runs after the count is gone (line 522-523). A background subagent's `turn.step` that lands in that window finds no loop entry, no probe mark and no in-flight description, so a call whose description reads `/x` is registered as a forked skill 'x' and writes a second, wrong usage row. The window is a few awaited atom updates, but it is the exact case the new guard exists for.

Also (runtime): `dispatching` is keyed by description text only, not by loop. While any `Agent` call with description `/x` is in flight, a genuine forked skill `x` whose loop first requests during that time is classified as that call's loop (line 323) and, since it is then marked probed, is never registered, so its usage row is lost. Rare (needs concurrent Agent call with a slash-form description and a fork of the same name), but the doc at lines 276-280 states the rule as absolute.

Also (overall): whileDispatching (tracker.ts:287-296) removes the description from `dispatching` as soon as `next(e)` returns, before recordResult's registerLoop (tracker.ts:361, 258-259) writes the loop into loopsAtom. noticeFork reads loopsAtom (tracker.ts:320) before awaiting `$.agent.list()` and checks `dispatching` only after it (tracker.ts:323). A background loop whose first request finished while the launch was still in flight can read an empty loopsAtom, then find `dispatching` already cleared, and register a fork; both registrations then write loopsAtom[loopId], the last one wins, and the other run is never completed (for a claimed pr-review/pr-team background dispatch its agent stays pending in the band). The README's limitation text (plugins/agent-watcher/README.md:322-324) states the background case is skipped once the launch result returns, without this gap. The window is small in practice, since the first request normally ends long after the launch returns.
fix: Keep the description counted until the result is folded: call `recordResult` inside the `whileDispatching` callback (for example `const r = await whileDispatching(e.description, async () => { const x = await next(e); await recordResult(...).catch(noop); return x })`), then update the `dispatching` doc to 'until its result is recorded'.

Alternatively have `noticeFork` skip when a loop is not yet registered but a background launch is pending, by registering the loop id first and leaving the description count to cover only the synchronous case.
State the limit in the FORK_DESCRIPTION/dispatching docs (a same-text fork during an in-flight call is attributed to the call).
Or leave the probe mark unset when the description matched `dispatching`, so the loop's next request is looked up again once the call returns.

In noticeFork, re-read loopsAtom after the `$.agent.list()` await and return when the loop is already mapped; and in registerFork make the loopsAtom insert conditional (skip and drop the run when an entry exists).
Or keep the description in `dispatching` until recordResult has registered the loop (wrap `next(e)` and `recordResult` together), plus the post-list loopsAtom re-check.

minor.name: Cost bullet says every other subagent loop costs a list lookup; registered background loops skip it
minor.summary: plugins/agent-watcher/README.md:319 says "Every other subagent loop costs one `$.agent.list()` lookup on its first request". noticeFork (tracker.ts:320) returns before the lookup for any loop already in `loopsAtom`, so a background `Agent` launch registered by recordResult pays none, while a resumed loop pays again (probedLoops is cleared at turn end, tracker.ts:389) and a rejected lookup is repeated on later requests.
fix: Reword to: "Every subagent loop not already registered as a background launch costs one `$.agent.list()` lookup per run of turns (repeated while the list rejects); only a forked skill's loop resolves the project there too."

minor.name: noticeFork now lists agents in non-harness projects, against the module's 'active only' contract
minor.summary:
The reorder (line 321 before resolveWatch at 325) means every new subagent loop pays `$.agent.list()` and gets a probe mark even outside a project holding `.claude/harness.json`, while the module docstring (lines 23-25) says the core is active only in such a project. The noticeFork doc admits the cost ('pays the list lookup alone') but the module-level contract is not adjusted, and the pre-change code returned before the list call there.

Also (runtime): markProbed now runs after `await $.agent.list()` rather than before any await (the old firstProbe). The retry-on-rejection behavior is intended, but a second concurrent `noticeFork` for the same loop would pass the line 320 check and double-register; the doc does not state the one-request-at-a-time assumption. Also the noticeFork docstring (line 315-316) still says 'On the loop's first request', while the code and the lifecycle comment (line 540) now retry on the next request when the list rejects.

Also (runtime): registerFork's doc says 'the run is dropped when either step throws'. If `registerLoop` fails on its runsAtom update after the loopsAtom update succeeded, the run is dropped but `loopsAtom[loopId]` still maps to the dropped run; the loop end then folds into a missing run, and the stale mapping is only removed at that end. Failure needs an atom write error, so low likelihood.
fix: Reword the module docstring so that 'active only in a harness project' covers the registration, not the lookup.
Or resolve the watch first (cheap, cached by resolveWatch if it is) and only then list, restoring the previous no-op outside a harness project.
Edit the noticeFork docstring to 'On the loop's first request the agent list answers for (the next one when the lookup rejects)'.
Optionally re-check `probedLoops.has(loopId)` after the list await before calling registerFork.
In the catch, also remove `loopId` from `loopsAtom` (`update($, loopsAtom, ...)` filter) before rethrowing.
Or narrow the doc to say the loop mapping is cleared at its end.

minor.name: A permanently refused agent list is asked on every subagent request
minor.summary: A rejected `$.agent.list()` leaves no probe mark (tracker.ts:321-322), so an engine that refuses the call (unsupported, or denied by another plugin) gets one list call per model request of every subagent loop, in every project, including outside harness projects where the lookup previously never ran. The README's cost note (plugins/agent-watcher/README.md:319-320) says one lookup per loop.
fix: Count refusals per loop (or process-wide) and mark the loop probed after a small number of failed lookups, e.g. 2-3; state the bound in the README cost note.
Or keep the unbounded retry and amend README lines 164-165 and 319-320 to say a refused lookup is retried on every request.

minor.name: Negative resolve-no-project assertion has no positive control
minor.summary:
'a loop that is not a fork resolves no project' only asserts that no `--git-common-dir` git call was made. Nothing in the file shows that a fork does make that call, so the assertion would still pass if the project lookup stopped issuing that argv (for example if `mainCheckoutOf` changed its git arguments). The test cannot fail for that reason.

Also (tests): The tests at 742-748 and 774-781 end with an `await loopEnd(...)` after their last assertion. The loop is never registered, so the call only runs `probedLoops.delete(loopId)` in recordLoopEnd, which clears module-level state in core/tracker.ts. The reason is not written anywhere, and a later edit that drops the 'unused' call would leave a probe mark behind for other tests that reuse a loop id. Other new tests (729-740, 750-762) rely on the same cleanup.
fix: In 'a forked skill loop logs one row under the skill it names' (or a sibling fork test), add expect(seen.git.some(argv => argv.includes('--git-common-dir'))).toBe(true) after the steps, so the negative case has a paired positive.
Add a one-line comment at each trailing loopEnd (for example '// clears the probe mark so later tests see a fresh loop') or move the cleanup into a small helper named for that purpose.

minor.name: Commit message claims a schema `source` field and bubble-memo changes that the diff does not contain
minor.summary:
Head commit 1da0183 says the agent_usage schema gains a new `source` field and that `bubble-memo` and `roast-my-code` contracts gained on-request review sections. At the head the schema change is a description-only edit (agent_usage.schema.json:5, no `source` property), no bubble-memo file changed, and the roast-my-code edit only moves pasted code and the `Developer guidance:` line. The actual changes (in-flight `Agent` description guard, retry on a rejected agent-list lookup, project resolution deferred to forks, registerFork rollback) go unmentioned.

Also (overall): The head commit message says the agent_usage schema gains a new `source` field to tell regular agent calls from forked skills, and that the `bubble-memo` skill contract was refactored with on-request review sections. The schema diff changes only the top-level `description` string (no `source` property; additionalProperties stays false), and no bubble-memo file is in the diff. The roast-my-code change is a one-bullet prompt layout clarification, not an on-request review section.
fix: Rewrite the commit message / PR description: drop the `source` field and bubble-memo claims; describe the `dispatching` guard against `/token` Agent descriptions, the retry when `$.agent.list()` rejects, project resolution only for forks, the registerFork rollback, and the roast-my-code pasted-code ordering.

Rewrite the commit/PR text: agent-watcher no longer takes an in-flight Agent call whose description is a single /token for a forked skill, retries a refused agent-list lookup, resolves the project only for a fork loop; the usage schema description mentions fork rows; roast-my-code places Developer guidance after pasted code. Drop the `source` field and bubble-memo claims.
